title: Baddha Kundalakesa
speaker: Seiu Hannah Sullivan
summary: Seiu Hannah Sullivan tells the story of Baddha Kundalakesa, a woman ancestor from the Therigatha who lived in Magadha around 500 BCE, as part of Seiu's continuing practice of honoring women ancestors. Baddha falls for a thief she has pardoned, survives his attempt to throw her off a cliff for her jewelry, and becomes a Jain renunciate whose hair grows back curly. Over fifty years of wandering she becomes a famed debater who marks each town with a sand pile and a rose apple stick. Seiu connects this to Zen mondo and shosan. Baddha falls silent when Shariputra asks "What is the one?" and he takes her to the Buddha. Seiu closes with her death poem about kissing every inch of every road, then offers two questions for small groups.

Bada remained silent, intrigued by what he was inquiring about.

All of those would have been a good answer.
But Bada decided not to formulate an answer, and thereby lost the debate, because she knew she'd found what she'd been searching for in all those years of wandering.
